question: The sixth revision of Directive 2004/37/EC1 states in a recital that hazardous medicinal products (HMPs) fall within the Directive’s scope in so far as they contain carcinogenic, mutagenic or reprotoxic substances. However, the handling of HMPs is not listed as a process in Annex I to the Directive.

Healthcare worker representatives point out that a recital does not provide employers or labour inspectorates with a clear legal basis for compliance and enforcement. Therefore, it remains unclear for employers whether, and how, the Directive’s requirements apply to the preparation, administration and disposal of HMPs. An estimated 12.7 million healthcare workers are potentially exposed. 1.
Does the Commission intend to include the handling of HMPs as a process in Annex I in its proposal for the seventh revision of the Directive?
Will it request an opinion from the Advisory Committee on Safety and Health at Work on this and, if so, what is the timeline?

Directive 2004/37/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council of 29 April 2004 on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to carcinogens or mutagens at work (Sixth individual Directive within the meaning of Article 16(1) of Council Directive 89/391/EEC) (OJ L 158, 30.4.2004, p. 50, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/dir/2004/37/oj). 1
